scope: Source review of local candidate token, permanent vault, exact-input router and focused token tests

findings.issue: Native settlement did not clear a previously synced ERC20 in the same transaction, allowing a composability denial of service.
findings.regression_test: NovaPreSyncBuyer performs ERC20 sync then router buy in the same transaction; parent integration runner verifies.

reviewed_guards: Vault launch checks exact hook poolManager/nova/initializer/fee/tickSpacing/initialSqrtPriceX96/poolId before any pool initialization
Vault only permits one initialization with exactly1ETH; constructor requires at least99.9pct of each fixed budget enters the LP
Vault callback requires immutable manager and one-shot authorization consumed before interactions
Vault only performs positive liquidity addition with fixed range/salt/amount and matches exact precomputed debt
No principal/fee/dust withdrawal, approval, arbitrary execution, ownership or upgrade path
Router bounds exact input to int128, checks deadline/minimum output and requires full fill
Router callback requires immutable manager and active nonreentrant entry; payouts are directed to the caller encoded by router
Native payout reentry cannot reenter buy/sell while outer trade active
Token exposes standard ERC20 functions plus fixed supply constant; no external mint/burn/admin/upgrade selectors
deliberate_limitations: Inference failure reverts buys and sells; immutable deployment cannot be patched in place
Genesis LP fees and dust are permanently inaccessible as well as principal
Standard ERC20 transferability permits third-party pools not governed by this hook
Router deployment configuration must be verified against vault/hook; constructor currently checks addresses have code but does not independently read hook bindings
